questions.explanation: 'Ask' takes object + to-infinitive: 'asked me to water'.
questions.q: She asked ___ to water her plants.

questions.explanation: 'Tell' takes an object before the infinitive: 'told us to finish'.
questions.q: The teacher ___ us to finish by Friday.

questions.explanation: 'Advise' takes object + to-infinitive: 'advised me to rest'.
options: He advised to me to rest.
He advised that I to rest.
questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.

questions.explanation: 'Persuade' takes object + to-infinitive; 'suggest' and 'recommend' do not.
questions.q: They ___ him to join the team.

questions.explanation: 'Warn' takes object + (not) to-infinitive: 'warned us not to smoke'.
questions.q: The sign warned ___ not to smoke.

questions.explanation: 'Allow' takes object + to-infinitive: 'allow her to stay'.
questions.q: Her parents won't allow ___ to stay out late.

questions.explanation: 'Encourage' takes object + to-infinitive.
options: The coach encouraged to the players to try harder.
The coach encouraged the players try harder.
The coach encouraged that the players try harder.
The coach encouraged the players to try harder.
questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.

questions.explanation: 'Want' takes object + to-infinitive: 'want you to be careful'.
questions.q: I want ___ to be careful on the ice.

questions.explanation: 'Expect' takes object + to-infinitive: 'expected everyone to attend'.
questions.q: The manager expected ___ to attend the briefing.

questions.explanation: 'Tell' needs an object before the infinitive: 'told us to use'.
questions.q: They ___ us to use the back entrance.

questions.explanation: 'Make' takes object + bare infinitive: 'made me laugh'.
questions.q: Find the sentence with a mistake.

questions.explanation: 'Enable' takes object + to-infinitive: 'enables us to work'.
questions.q: The new software enables ___ to work from home.

questions.explanation: 'Force' takes object + to-infinitive: 'forced him to practice'.
questions.q: She forced her son ___ daily.

questions.explanation: 'Let' takes object + bare infinitive; the others need 'to'.
questions.q: The teacher ___ the students leave early.

questions.explanation: 'Order' takes object + to-infinitive: 'ordered me to sit down'.
options: He ordered to me to sit down.
He ordered that me to sit down.
He ordered me to sit down.
questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.

questions.explanation: 'Convince' takes object + to-infinitive; 'suggest', 'propose' and 'recommend' do not.
questions.q: We ___ them to reconsider the offer.

questions.explanation: 'Advise' takes object + to-infinitive: 'advised her to avoid'.
questions.q: The doctor ___ her to avoid stress.

questions.explanation: 'Remind' takes object + to-infinitive: 'reminded him to lock'.
questions.q: I ___ him to lock the door.

questions.explanation: 'Let' takes the bare infinitive: 'let me go'.
questions.q: Find the sentence with a mistake.

questions.explanation: 'Urge' takes object + to-infinitive: 'urged people to vote'.
questions.q: The campaign urged ___ to vote.

topic: Verb + object + infinitive (want him to go)
